title: Threshold power identity
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. For real numbers $\epsilon,\eta>0$ and an integer $k\ge0$, suppose the total influence $I(f)$ is positive, where $I(f)$ is the sum over coordinates of the expected squared discrete derivative of the real-valued sign function $f$. Then $$\left(\left(\frac{\epsilon}{I(f)}\left(\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}\right)^k\right)^{1+\eta}\right)^{1/(1+\eta)}=\frac{\epsilon}{I(f)}\left(\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}\right)^k.$$
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube to the signs
The total influence of $f$ is positive
